text:
Sunshine has done its job this Monday. We're already in the mid 60s with clear skies, and the afternoon tops out near 68, which is well above normal for early November. A high-pressure system sliding off to our south is turning the flow southerly and pulling in the mild air. With the sun setting around 4:40, the best window for a walk or a ride is the next couple of hours, and a light layer will do.

Clouds thicken tonight, and it stays mild with a low around 52. Tuesday turns gray and cooler, with a high near 60. A few showers could pass through, mostly from about 2 to 5 in the afternoon. They'd be light, under a tenth of an inch, so a jacket is enough and you won't need to cancel anything. The models lean a little wetter than the official forecast, so I'd keep an umbrella handy.

Then it warms up again. Wednesday looks like the warmest day of the week, in the low 70s and close to record territory. Steady rain arrives Thursday, heaviest Thursday night.

AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: High pressure 1034 mb centered over the mid Atlantic coast this afternoon will continue to drift slowly eastward into the Atlantic Ocean this week, turning flow over northern New York and Vermont more southerly. This will result in a warming trend today through Wednesday, although some shower chances towards the Canadian border Tuesday afternoon may stunt warmth locally, particularly along the international border. Highs on Tuesday will be widespread 60s with overnight lows in the mid 40s to lower 50s. The warmest day of the week will be Wednesday with deep layer winds advecting warm air out of the south/southeasterly directions under mostly clear to partly cloudy skies. Low and mid 70s are anticipated for Wednesday afternoon, with lows that night as warm as the 40s to mid 50s. A few spots could exceed their daily records, particularly in the St. Lawrence Valley of New York. Warmth recedes slightly on Thursday, but conditions remain warm with widespread highs in the 60s. KEY MESSAGE 2: A weak wave will be moving along a ridge's northern periphery Tuesday and Tuesday night, bringing rain shower chances mainly to northern New York and the northern half of Vermont. Amounts will be light given that it will be moving into a ridge, with projected rainfall up to 0.15 inches at most, highest along the international border. Breezy southerly winds are also likely in north south oriented valleys Tuesday night after the showers pass through. Then on Thursday, rain will spread eastward through our region, driven by a frontal boundary attached to an elongated low pressure stretched from the Great Lakes to Quebec, Canada. Winds will be breezy out of the south with gusts up to 20-25 mph, particularly Thursday morning ahead of steady precipitation. Most likely period for rainfall is Thursday for northern New York, then Thursday night for Vermont. Some upslope flow could mean highest precipitation amounts on western slopes of the Adirondacks and Greens. Precipitation amounts in 24 hours reaching a half inch or more look fairly unlikely, with perhaps the best chance of these higher amounts in the Adirondacks and southern half of Vermont, closest to the stream of moisture coming off the Gulf. All precipitation should be rain with this system, and we're not expecting a dramatic cooldown until at least this weekend. More on the extended forecast below. KEY MESSAGE 3: Following Friday's frontal passage, we'll have several days of active weather. A secondary low pressure forms downstream of the front. This secondary low will meander eastward with precip rotating around the center of the low. At this point, we can't nail down the timing but expect chance to likely rain from Friday evening through Sunday. One of the questions we will need to answer is how quickly that secondary low moves. NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-02T18:01:00Z — same caveat): Warming up with a south breeze, partly sunny skies Monday — Most of the upcoming workweek looks mild for early November, with highs in the 60s for several days! Monday afternoon will feature a blend of sun and clouds. The warmup continues, thanks to an active south breeze. Highs reach the 60s to around 70. Tonight will be mostly cloudy and not too chilly, with lows in the 40s to around 50. Tuesday (Election Day) brings a mostly cloudy sky with passing light showers and perhaps a period of steady rain in northern areas, as a warm front lifts through. Highs will be near 60. Southern Vermont can expect more breaks of sun, with highs closer to 70. Wednesday looks to be the warmest day, as highs reach the low to mid-70s region-wide, along with a mostly sunny sky and an active south breeze. After that, an area of low pressure brings the potential for beneficial rain late week. Scattered showers are likely Thursday, especially by afternoon. Showers look to linger Friday, especially south. Highs reach the 60s both days. This weekend turns cooler, an an upper-level low sends highs back to the upper 40s. Expect lots of clouds with additional showers possible, especially on Saturday.
